title: Paper trading agents echoed peer wording without a detectable immediate trade shift
summary: In a seven-day paper trading study with 200 agents across four model families, later-starting board agents reused peers' phrases 6.8 percentage points more often when they could see a fresh post. A timing-based comparison found no detectable same-morning shift in matching trades, with an estimate of 2.4 points and a 95% interval of −4.1 to 9.3.
ai_technology: Opus 5.5; GPT-6.1 Sol; Grok 4.6; DeepSeek V4 Pro

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 primary HTML §§1–2.3, 4, 5.1 and 8.2, Appendix A and C.4

evidence.tested: Timing-based comparisons found 6.8 percentage points more same-morning eight-word phrase reuse for pairs with an opportunity to read a recent peer post (95% interval 1.7–11.8, 68 board group mornings). In a separate comparison subtracting timing differences in isolated groups, same-direction orders in the same stock differed by 2.4 points (95% interval −4.1 to 9.3).
evidence.unknown: The study used one group per communication regime and model family, with only seven trading days and simulated fills at live prices. Timing was not randomized. The interval leaves room for some short-run effects and says nothing about market impact.
evidence.ai_role: Four learned model families ran separate paper trading accounts and produced peer messages while retaining independent decisions. Frozen views and time-stamped paper orders made phrase and order comparisons possible.
